changes.summary: Pennsylvania's new annual report ($7) has had no dissolution penalties for 2025 and 2026 reports; full enforcement, including administrative dissolution, begins with 2027 reports.
Federal definition change: finished hemp-derived consumables above 0.4 mg total THC per container are treated as marijuana under federal law, affecting hemp and intoxicating-hemp businesses.
Virginia adult-use retail sales are reported to be slated to begin July 1, 2027; retail licensing legislation was vetoed in 2025, so this date is not confirmed.

A DOJ/DEA order rescheduled state-licensed medical cannabis to Schedule III; adult-use cannabis remains Schedule I and a broader rescheduling proceeding is pending. IRC §280E relief applies going forward to state-licensed medical operators.
Delaware LLC, LP and general partnership annual tax rises from $300 to $400, first reflected in payments due June 1, 2027.
Louisiana Secretary of State commercial fees increased under Act 921 (annual reports $35; registered LLP filings and renewals $155).
Rhode Island sole proprietorships and general partnerships register trade names with the Secretary of State instead of city or town clerks, with mandatory annual renewal.
Delaware trade name registration moved from county Prothonotary offices to a statewide registry run by the Division of Revenue.
Alabama repealed the Secretary of State corporate annual report requirement (Act 2024-213).
Oklahoma franchise tax eliminated beginning with tax year 2024.
Form 1099-NEC reporting threshold rises from $600 to $2,000 for payments made after 2025.
Washington cannabis producer, processor and retailer license fees increased under House Bill 2681.
Kansas Secretary of State announced reduced fees for biennial information reports; the new amounts are not yet reflected in the bundled data.
